question: What is the minimum turnover requirement?
expected_answer: Average annual turnover of at least Rs. 74 crore over the last five financial years, with specified weightages.
actual_answer:
The minimum turnover requirement is an average annual turnover of at least Rs. 74.00 Crore (50% of PAC) over the last five financial years (2021-22 to 2025-26), with past years’ turnover adjusted using the specified weightages to the 2025-26 price level. In case of a Joint Venture, at least one partner must meet this criterion.

This requirement is explicitly stated as:
- “The bidder should have Average Annual Turnover equal to or more than Rs. 74.00 Crore (50% of PAC) in last 5 financial years… In case of Joint Venture bidders, at least one partner should meet these criteria.” [S2]

The supporting form for calculating weighted turnover is provided in Form 2A. [S4]

question: What is the project completion period?
expected_answer: 18 months, including the rainy season, from the date of the contract agreement.
actual_answer:
The stipulated project completion period is 18 months (including rainy season) from the date of signing of the contract agreement/date of agreement.

This is described consistently as the “time for completion” or “period for completion of construction” in the tender documents and is stated not to exceed 18 months.

Relevant clauses:
- Volume I: “shall not exceed 18 Months including rainy seasons from the date of signing of contract agreement.” [S3]
- Volume II: “Shall not exceed 18 months including rainy season from the date of agreement.” [S4]
- Volume II: the “period for completion of construction in NIT” is the period up to issue of completion certificate, over which a 60‑month defects liability period applies beyond the 18‑month completion period. [S2]

Thus, the project completion period is 18 months from the agreement/signing date, including rainy seasons.

question: What are the eligibility criteria for a joint venture?
expected_answer: The joint venture must satisfy applicable qualification criteria and comply with JV agreement and authorization requirements.
actual_answer:
Based on the provided passages, the eligibility criteria for a joint venture are:

1. General competence and experience
- Joint ventures must be “competent & experienced contractor qualifying on the financial, Physical and experience criteria detailed hereinafter.” [S5]
- This means the JV must collectively meet the Project Pre‑Qualification (P.Q.) criteria specified in the tender.

2. Compliance with P.Q. / minimum qualifying criteria
- “The Bidder should meet qualifying criteria as stipulated in the tender document P.Q. criteria. Failure to comply with this requirement will result in rejection of the joint venture’s bid.” [S1]
- “All the partners collectively must meet the criteria specified in full. Failure to comply with this requirement will result in rejection of the joint venture’s bid.” [S3]
- Thus, for eligibility, the combined figures of all JV partners must fully meet the minimum qualifying criteria.

3. Debarment / historical performance
- For historical poor performance, each JV partner must satisfy the same condition as a single bidder: “Bidder should not have been debarred or contract terminated by MPSEB, its six successor companies during the last five years counted up to the date of opening of Bid… it is clarified that… debarring/blacklisting should not be alive / active on the date of opening of tender.” [S2]
- The eligibility table specifies that this requirement “must meet requirement” for “All Partners Combined”, “Lead Partner” and “Other Partner”. [S2]
- Therefore, no JV partner may have an active debarment/blacklisting from MPSEB or its successor companies as of the bid opening date, and any past debarment must have expired per the conditions stated.

4. Joint venture agreement and legal status
To be eligible, the JV must have an appropriate and binding JV agreement:
- “a copy of the Joint Venture Agreement entered into by the partners shall be submitted with the bid.” [S1]
- “The joint venture agreement should indicate precisely the role of all members of J.V. in respect of planning, design, construction equipment, key personnel, work execution, and financing of the project. All members of JV should have active participation in execution during the currency of the contract. This should not be varied/modified subsequently without prior approval of the employer;” [S3]
- “The joint venture agreement should be registered, so as to be legally valid and binding on all partners;” [S3]
- “Attach the agreement among all partners of the joint venture [and which is legally binding on all partners], which shows the requirements as indicated in the Instructions to Bidders’.” [S3]

5. Lead partner and performance security
- “The performance security of a Joint Venture shall be in the name of the Lead Partner /joint venture.” [S1]
- “The performance security of a Joint Venture shall be in the name of the partner Lead Partner /joint venture.” [S3]

6. Authority of bid signatory
- “Attach the power of attorney of the partners authorizing the Bid signatory (ies) on behalf of the joint venture.” [S1]
- “Attach the power of attorney of the partners authorizing the Bid signatory (i.e.) on behalf of the joint venture.” [S3]

7. Defined participation of partners
- The JV must furnish detailed participation information for each partner (financial, planning, equipment, key personnel, execution of work) as per the format: “Furnish details of participation proposed in the joint venture as below: DETAILS OF PARTICIPATION IN THE JOINT VENTURE…” [S1]
- The JV agreement must show “the role of all members of J.V. in respect of planning, design, construction equipment, key personnel, work execution, and financing of the project.” [S3]

8. Nature of joint and several responsibility
- By definition in this tender, a JV is only acceptable if all parties accept joint and several liability: “Joint Venture is an arrangement in which two or more parties enter into an agreement for the purpose of executing a specific task/project and all parties shall be jointly and severally responsible to incur all the liabilities under that task/project, if awarded.” [S1]

In summary, a joint venture is eligible only if (a) all partners collectively satisfy the stated P.Q. criteria, (b) no partner is under active debarment/blacklisting from MPSEB or its successors at bid opening, and (c) the JV has a properly registered, legally binding agreement defining roles, active participation, joint and several liability, performance security arrangements, power of attorney for bid signatories, and detailed participation information.

question: What documents are required to prove it?
expected_answer: Documents required to establish the eligibility criteria.
actual_answer:
Based on the passages provided, the tender’s eligibility criteria (at least the “Historical Poor Performance of Bidders” criterion) must be proven with the following documents:

1. **Form 4A for historical performance**  
   - For the eligibility factor "Historical Poor Performance of Bidders" (bidder not debarred / contract not terminated in the specified way), the tender explicitly requires **Form 4A** as the documentation to prove compliance. [S1]

2. **Technical Schedules (Forms 1 to 8) supported by certificates**  
   - The pre‑qualification document (Volume‑I) must be filled in the prescribed proforma as Technical Schedule **Form 1 to Form 8**, and these formats must be **supported by certificates** wherever necessary, signed by an officer not below the rank of Executive Engineer. These certificates must be translated into English and attested if issued in another Indian language. [S2]
   - Bidders must attach **all necessary documents like balance sheets, bank certificates, experience certificates and information of work in hand** with the prequalification document. [S2]

3. **Documents in Envelope A (required for opening and eligibility check)**  
   To have the bid opened and considered, the following must be provided in Envelope A:
   - **Earnest Money (valid bid security)** in one of the approved forms. [S3][S5]
   - **Copy of registration certificate** and **valid “A” Class electrical contractor license**. [S3][S5]
   - **Affidavit as per Annexure–1** and **additional affidavit as per Annexure–2**. [S3][S5]
   - **Power of Attorney (PoA)**. [S3][S5]
   - **JV related documents**, if the bidder is a joint venture (with reference to Clause 4.5 of Section I). [S3][S5]

4. **Documents in Envelope B (pre‑qualification / eligibility support)**  
   Envelope B must contain the pre‑qualification document (Volume‑I) showing eligibility, supported by certificates and other documents:
   - Pre‑qualification document (Volume‑I) with **Forms 1 to 8**. [S2][S5]
   - Supporting **certificates** signed by an officer not below the rank of Executive Engineer (translated and attested if needed). [S2][S5]
   - **Balance sheets, bank certificates, experience certificates, information of work in hand, etc.** attached with the pre‑qualification document. [S2][S5]

These are the documents explicitly identified in the supplied passages as required to prove compliance with the tender’s eligibility criteria and to have the bid considered responsive and pre‑qualified.
